T: Three days to get home. Snacks for every leg.
D: An ad man and a chatty shower curtain ring salesman try to get home for Thanksgiving.
P: Serve the snacks when Del pulls out his shower curtain rings.
S: the motel room they're forced to share
Salted peanuts, pretzels, chocolate bars and beef jerky tipped into a bowl, like the motel vending machine.
Del's sample case of curtain rings
Onions sliced into rings, soaked in buttermilk, dipped in beer batter, fried at 185C until puffed and golden.
Truck stop smoky pepper beef jerky
the long haul across the Midwest

Thin strips of topside marinated in soy, Worcestershire, brown sugar and smoked paprika, dried slowly in the oven until chewy, finished with cracked pepper. Freeze 600g beef topside for 1 hour, then slice 3mm thick with the grain. Mix 80ml soy sauce, 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp cracked black pepper. Marinate the beef overnight. Pat dry, lay on wire racks over trays and dry at 75C with the oven door slightly open for 3 to 4 hours until leathery but bendy. Cool and store in a jar.
M: they finally make it home for Thanksgiving
Turkey breast brined and roasted at 170C to 70C, sliced, in soft slider buns with cranberry sauce, a square of baked stuffing and a spoon of gravy.
the bus ride to St Louis after the train dies

A thick chuck patty griddled to medium with melted cheddar, grilled onions, pickles and mustard in a toasted bun, with a stack of beer-battered onion rings. Shape 700g chuck mince into 4 thick patties and season well. Cook 1 sliced onion on the griddle with butter for 10 minutes. Griddle the patties 4 minutes a side, lay a slice of cheddar on each and cover for 1 minute. Toast 4 burger buns. Build with grilled onions, pickles and mustard. Serve with 500g frozen beer-battered onion rings baked at 220C for 15 minutes.
W: Roast pumpkin purée whisked with eggs, brown sugar, cream, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg, baked in a blind-baked case at 170C for 50 minutes. Whipped cream.
K: Home for Thanksgiving apple cider punch
Neal finally walks in the door for Thanksgiving

Cloudy apple juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves and orange, spiked with bourbon for the grown-ups, served warm in mugs with a cinnamon stick. Put 1.5L cloudy apple juice, 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves, 1 sliced orange and 2 tbsp brown sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer and keep it there for 15 minutes without boiling. Strain into a jug. Pour into 4 mugs, add 30ml bourbon to each adult mug, and serve with a fresh cinnamon stick.

edition.tagline: Three days to get home. Snacks for every leg.
edition.cue: Serve the snacks when Del pulls out his shower curtain rings.

s.note: Salted peanuts, pretzels, chocolate and beef jerky in one shared bowl.
s.how: Tip 60g salted peanuts, 60g pretzels, 60g chopped chocolate bars and 40g beef jerky into a shared bowl. Mix gently and divide between four people for the motel snack break.

s.note: Buttermilk soaked onion rings in crisp golden beer batter.
s.how: Slice 2 brown onions into thick rings and soak in 150ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Whisk 120g plain flour, 150ml cold lager and 1/4 tsp salt into a batter. Drain the rings, dip in the batter and fry in small batches in neutral oil at 185°C for 3 to 4 minutes until puffed and golden. Drain and serve hot.

m.note: Roast turkey with cranberry, baked stuffing and gravy in soft buns.
m.how: Dissolve 30g salt in 1 litre cold water. Submerge 700g turkey breast and refrigerate for 6 hours. Drain, pat dry and roast at 170°C conventional for about 50 to 60 minutes, until the centre reaches 70°C and stays at that temperature for 2 minutes. Rest 15 minutes and slice. Prepare 150g stuffing mix with the packet's water amount, spread in a small baking dish and bake beside the turkey for 25 minutes, then cut into 8 squares. Make gravy by melting 20g butter, stirring in 20g flour for 1 minute and whisking in 300ml chicken stock; simmer 5 minutes. Fill 8 soft slider buns with turkey, 80g cranberry sauce, stuffing squares and a spoonful of gravy. Serve two each.

w.note: Spiced roast pumpkin custard in pastry, served with whipped cream.
w.how: Roast 450g peeled pumpkin at 200°C conventional for 30 minutes until soft, then purée and measure 300g. Line a 20cm pie dish with 250g sweet shortcrust pastry. Blind-bake with baking paper and weights at 180°C for 15 minutes, remove the weights and bake 5 minutes more. Whisk the pumpkin purée with 2 eggs, 80g brown sugar, 100ml thickened cream, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground ginger and 1/8 tsp nutmeg. Pour into the crust and bake at 170°C for 50 minutes until just set. Cool, then serve four portions with another 100ml cream softly whipped.
